Changing your position on the road involves changing lanes or overtaking and passing another vehicle.

statements.text: DEFINE passing IS a lane change THAT is made to move past a slower vehicle

statements.text: FACT not all vehicles travel at the same speed, although all public roads have speed limits

sources.quote: While all public roads have speed limits, not all vehicles travel at the same speed. For example, cyclists, road service vehicles and drivers ahead that are preparing to turn are usually slower than the through traffic. You may want to pass some slow-moving vehicles when you are following them.

statements.text: FACT cyclists, road service vehicles and drivers ahead that are preparing to turn are [?usually] slower than the through traffic

sources.quote: While all public roads have speed limits, not all vehicles travel at the same speed. For example, cyclists, road service vehicles and drivers ahead that are preparing to turn are usually slower than the through traffic. You may want to pass some slow-moving vehicles when you are following them.

flags.note: Hedged; the handbook does not say when these road users are not slower.

statements.text: FACT a driver following [?some] slow-moving vehicles may want to pass those vehicles

sources.quote: While all public roads have speed limits, not all vehicles travel at the same speed. You may want to pass some slow-moving vehicles when you are following them.

flags.note: The handbook does not say which slow-moving vehicles a driver may want to pass.

statements.note: "You may want to pass" is motivation, not a permission, so it is written as a FACT.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass another vehicle UNLESS the driver is [?sure] the pass can be made without danger to the driver or others

sources.quote: Never overtake and pass another vehicle unless you are sure you can do so without danger to yourself or others.

flags.note: The handbook gives no test for when a driver can be sure that a pass carries no danger.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a moving snow plow under any conditions

sources.quote: Don't pass moving snow plows under any conditions.

flags.note: An absolute ban with no legal marker; the handbook does not say whether it is law.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass WHEN the driver is [?in doubt]

sources.quote: If in doubt, do not pass.

flags.note: The handbook does not say what doubt should stop a pass.

statements.text: TO pass a vehicle

steps.text: signal left to show that the driver wants to pass AND check that the way is clear ahead and behind

WATCH FOR bicycles and small vehicles that may be hidden from view in front of the vehicle to be passed AND WATCH FOR vehicles that may be turning left in front of the driver AND WATCH FOR vehicles or pedestrians entering the road from another road or driveway
signal that the driver wants to move back into the original lane WHEN the driver has passed the vehicle
move back into the original lane WHEN the driver can see the entire front of the vehicle being passed in the inside mirror
IF the vehicle being passed speeds up THEN do not race AND return to the original lane

sources.quote: Here are the steps for passing a vehicle:
how to pass another vehicle

statements.text: a driver SHOULD change lanes WHEN passing ONLY IF the driver has first signalled

sources.quote: Change lanes only after signalling. After overtaking, signal that you want to move back into the lane you started from, and when you can see the entire front of the vehicle you are passing in your inside mirror, make the lane change.
Here are the steps for passing a vehicle:

statements.note: "When passing" comes from the heading (Passing) and the list lead m8; the step order of m8a repeats this.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT cut off a vehicle by suddenly moving in front of the vehicle WHEN passing

statements.note: "When passing" comes from the heading (Passing) and the list lead m8.

statements.text: a driver being passed MUST NOT speed up WHILE another driver is trying to pass the driver BECAUSE speeding up is dangerous

sources.quote: And do not speed up when another driver is trying to pass you. It is unlawful and dangerous.

flags.span: driving a motor vehicle to prevent another vehicle from passing

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass a vehicle WHEN the driver is within 30 m of a pedestrian crossover

sources.quote: Passing within 30 metres of a pedestrian crossover is not permitted.
You must not pass any vehicle within 30 metres of a pedestrian crossover.

flags.span: You must not pass any vehicle within 30 metres of a pedestrian crossover.
flags.note: Restated on the Stopping page (m16) as "must not pass any vehicle".

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass [?left of the centreline] WHEN the driver is [?30 m from] a bridge, viaduct or tunnel

sources.quote: Passing left of a centreline is not permitted 30 metres from a bridge, viaduct or tunnel.

flags.note: The ban is on passing that crosses to the left of the centreline, not on passing as such.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT attempt to pass WHEN (the driver is approaching the crest of a hill OR the driver is on a curve) AND the view of oncoming traffic is obstructed AND there is not [?enough] clear distance ahead to pass [?in safety]

sources.quote: Don't attempt to pass when approaching the crest of a hill or on a curve where your vision of oncoming traffic is obstructed and there is not enough clear distance ahead to pass in safety.

flags.note: No distance is given for enough clear distance.

statements.note: The obstructed view and the clear distance are read as applying to both the hill and the curve.

sources.quote: Motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds often need to pull to the left or right side of their lane to avoid dangerous road conditions or to be seen by other drivers. flags.note: Hedged; the handbook does not say how often.

sources.quote: Motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds often need to pull to the left or right side of their lane to avoid dangerous road conditions or to be seen by other drivers. Do not take this as an invitation to pass in the same lane. If you do want to pass these vehicles, do so by changing lanes.

sources.quote: Motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds often need to pull to the left or right side of their lane to avoid dangerous road conditions or to be seen by other drivers. how to pass another vehicle

sources.quote: When faster traffic wants to pass you, move to the right and let it pass in safety.

statements.force_from: imperative ("pay attention to oncoming traffic and move closer to the right side of the lane")

sources.quote: When being passed on an undivided road where the passing driver has pulled into the opposite lane, pay attention to oncoming traffic and move closer to the right side of the lane. statements.text: a driver being passed SHOULD be prepared to slow down to let the passing driver get in front of the driver more quickly WHEN the driver is on an undivided road AND the passing driver has pulled into the opposite lane BECAUSE this helps prevent a collision

sources.quote: When being passed on an undivided road where the passing driver has pulled into the opposite lane, pay attention to oncoming traffic and move closer to the right side of the lane. Be prepared to slow down to let the passing driver get in front of you more quickly to prevent a collision.

statements.note: The undivided-road condition comes from the first sentence of the passage.

statements.text: a truck driver MUST NOT drive in the far-left lane WHEN the driver is on one of [?many] high-speed roads with 3 or more lanes in each direction

sources.quote: On many high-speed roads with three or more lanes in each direction, trucks are not allowed to drive in the far left-hand lane. This means that the lane next to it is the truck passing lane. If you are in this lane and a truck wants to pass, move into the right-hand lane as soon as you can.
On many freeways with three or more lanes in each direction, large trucks cannot travel in the far left lane and must use the lane to the right for passing.

flags.note: The handbook does not say which of these roads have the ban.

flags.span: large trucks cannot travel in the far left lane
flags.note: Restated on the Freeway driving page (m91) for large trucks on many freeways.
m90 says "far left-hand lane" where m33 and m91 say "far left lane".

statements.note: "Trucks" (m90) and "large trucks" (m91) are taken as the same vehicles.

statements.text: FACT the lane next to the far-left lane is the truck passing lane WHEN trucks are not allowed in the far-left lane

sources.quote: On many high-speed roads with three or more lanes in each direction, trucks are not allowed to drive in the far left-hand lane. This means that the lane next to it is the truck passing lane. If you are in this lane and a truck wants to pass, move into the right-hand lane as soon as you can.

statements.text: a driver in the truck passing lane SHOULD move into the right-hand lane [?as soon as the driver can] WHEN a truck wants to pass

sources.quote: On many high-speed roads with three or more lanes in each direction, trucks are not allowed to drive in the far left-hand lane. This means that the lane next to it is the truck passing lane. If you are in this lane and a truck wants to pass, move into the right-hand lane as soon as you can.

flags.note: No time or distance is given.

statements.note: "This lane" is the truck passing lane named in the previous sentence.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD pass other vehicles with [?extra care] WHEN it is night

sources.quote: Be very careful when you pass other vehicles at night.

flags.note: "Be very careful" names no hazard or specific action.

steps.text: switch to low beams WHEN approaching the vehicle from behind
signal AND check the mirrors AND check the blind spot AND pull out to pass
switch on high beams WHEN moving alongside the vehicle being passed BECAUSE this lets the driver see more of the road ahead
move back into the right-hand lane WHEN the driver can see all of the front of the vehicle being passed in the inside mirror

sources.quote: If you have to pass and the way is clear, follow these steps:

flags.note: m43 says "rear view mirror" where m11 says "inside mirror".
m43 says "right lane" where other passages say "right-hand lane".

statements.text: FACT [?some] roads have special passing or climbing lanes

a passing or climbing lane

flags.note: The handbook does not say which roads have these lanes.

a passing or climbing lane

statements.note: The passing or climbing lane comes from the heading (Passing and climbing lanes).

sources.quote: Most passing is done on the left. You may pass on the right on multi-lane or one-way roads and when overtaking a streetcar or a left-turning vehicle.

m35 says "overtaking" for passing.

sources.quote: Passing on the right can be more dangerous than passing on the left.

statements.text: a truck driver MUST use the lane to the right of the far-left lane for passing WHEN the driver is driving a large truck on one of [?many] freeways with 3 or more lanes in each direction

sources.quote: On many freeways with three or more lanes in each direction, large trucks cannot travel in the far left lane and must use the lane to the right for passing.

flags.note: The handbook does not say which freeways have this rule.

statements.note: m90 calls this lane the truck passing lane.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD use low beams WHEN (it is night OR the driver is driving in [?poor conditions]) AND the driver is less than 60 m behind another vehicle UNLESS the driver is passing the other vehicle

sources.quote: Use your low beams when you are less than 60 metres behind another vehicle unless you are passing it.

flags.note: The heading does not say which conditions count as poor.

statements.note: Night and poor conditions come from the heading (Turn on headlights at night and in poor conditions).

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk BECAUSE a stopped vehicle may be a clue that a pedestrian is crossing

sources.quote: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. A stopped vehicle may be a clue that a pedestrian is crossing.

statements.text: a cyclist MAY use any part of the lane to discourage passing WHEN the lane is [?too narrow to be shared safely] ONLY IF using any part of the lane is [?necessary for safety]

sources.quote: Discourage passing where the lane is too narrow to be shared safely
However, they can use any part of the lane if necessary for safety, such as to:

flags.span: too narrow to be shared safely

statements.text: a driver of a motor vehicle MUST keep at least 1 m between the vehicle and the cyclist, [?where practical], WHILE passing a cyclist IF VIOLATED a fine AND 2 demerit points

sources.quote: When passing a cyclist, drivers of motor vehicles must maintain a minimum distance of one metre, where practical between their vehicle and the cyclist.

bike lane adjacent to parking bays

statements.text: a driver SHOULD change lanes to pass a cyclist WHEN it is [?possible]

sources.quote: Whenever possible, you should change lanes to pass.

flags.note: The handbook does not say when changing lanes is not possible.

flags.span: If you do want to pass these vehicles, do so by changing lanes.

statements.note: "A cyclist" comes from the heading (Cyclists) and the neighbouring passage m56.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT sound the horn [?unnecessarily] WHILE passing a cyclist BECAUSE the horn may frighten the cyclist and cause the cyclist to lose control

sources.quote: Do not sound your horn unnecessarily when you are overtaking a cyclist. It may frighten them and cause them to lose control. If you feel that you must use your horn, tap it quickly and lightly while you are still some distance away from the cyclist.

flags.note: The handbook does not say when the horn is necessary.
m60 says "overtaking" for passing.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD tap the horn quickly and lightly WHEN passing a cyclist AND the driver feels that the horn must be used WHILE the driver is still [?some distance] away from the cyclist

sources.quote: Do not sound your horn unnecessarily when you are overtaking a cyclist. It may frighten them and cause them to lose control. If you feel that you must use your horn, tap it quickly and lightly while you are still some distance away from the cyclist.

flags.note: No distance is given.

statements.note: "Must" here is the driver's own judgment, not a legal duty; "passing a cyclist" comes from the passage's first sentence.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT cut in [?closely] in front of a large vehicle WHEN passing the large vehicle BECAUSE cutting in this way is discourteous and dangerous AND it reduces the space cushion large vehicles require to stop [?safely]

sources.quote: When passing a large vehicle, do not cut in front closely. Not only is this discourteous, it is dangerous; it reduces the space cushion large vehicles require in order to stop safely. Allow more room when passing a large vehicle.

flags.note: No distance is given for cutting in closely.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD allow [?more room] WHEN passing a large vehicle

sources.quote: When passing a large vehicle, do not cut in front closely. Not only is this discourteous, it is dangerous; it reduces the space cushion large vehicles require in order to stop safely. Allow more room when passing a large vehicle.

flags.note: The handbook does not say how much more room, or more than what.

statements.text: FACT a large vehicle can create heavy air turbulence, due to factors such as air pressure and airflow

sources.quote: 6. Turbulence - Due to various factors such as air pressure and airflow, a large vehicle can create heavy air turbulence. This may affect your ability to control your vehicle when passing a large one.

statements.text: FACT the air turbulence created by a large vehicle may affect a driver's ability to control the vehicle WHEN the driver is passing the large vehicle

statements.note: "Them" is read as the horse-drawn vehicle from the heading (Horse-drawn vehicles).

statements.text: FACT in Ontario, school bus drivers and other witnesses can report vehicles that have illegally passed a school bus

vehicles travelling beside broken yellow lines

sources.quote: This placard indicates a long commercial vehicle, which is a double trailer and can be up to 40 metres in length. It is important to be able to recognize an LCV on the highway, based on rear signage, and anticipate both the extended length and limited speed when preparing to pass one on the highway.
Title: Long commercial vehicle (LCV) - Description: Long commercial vehicle (LCV)

statements.text: FACT a vehicle cannot accelerate as quickly WHEN it is towing a trailer

sources.quote: You cannot accelerate as quickly when you are towing a trailer. You also need more space because the length of your vehicle is much longer with a trailer attached. Before you pass, make sure you have enough time and room to complete the pass. Once you have passed, allow more room before you move back to your lane. Do not cut back into the lane too soon. This can cause your trailer to sway and make it difficult to control.

statements.note: "Cannot" describes ability here, not a prohibition.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD signal AND SHOULD pull over AND SHOULD let the other vehicles pass WHEN the driver is holding up a line of traffic

sources.quote: If you are holding up a line of traffic, signal, pull over and let the other vehicles pass. Fast-moving trucks and buses create a strong air disturbance behind them. If a large bus or truck passes you, the wall of wind behind it may whip your trailer to the side, pushing it out of control. When you experience this, do not brake. Carefully steer your vehicle and trailer back into position. A slight increase in speed may help.
